Linux Network Load Balancing

HOW TO CONFIGURE NETWORK BONDING (LACP) ON DEBIAN WHEEZY

First your switch/router has to support load balancing. Linux uses 802.3ad LACP at layer 2. If your switch is unable to support it, you are stuck with two IP's or basic fail-over. This is what is usually done with in your LAN.

Layer 3 load balancing can be done but it's based on the routing protocol you are using or NAT pool. This is usually what is used for WAN load balancing

Layer 4 load balancing, for your use case, is usually based on the service you are providing, not necessarily the service you are trying to access.

Almost all home consumer routers and switches don't do load balancing.

You definitely can't achieve a "true" single IP address bandwidth-sharing link to your switch/router unless your switch/router supports this feature. However, this being said, I read your comments and there might be another way to achieve your goals.

Your software might have an interface option, where you can confine all the traffic for that app to only use a certain interface. I know qBitTorrent allows forcing the application to only use a certain interface because most people only want to torrent over their VPN interface. Otherwise if the VPN connection went down, it would switch over the the direct hardline (non-encrypted) interface and start torrenting over that guy, so props for qBitTorrent for having this feature.

In your setup, if your software supports such a feature, you can static assign each port a separate IP address on your NIC card(s), and run each NIC on a separate cable to the switch. Your OS will probably pick one of them to be the primary connection, and that interface will be used for anything that you don't redirect through a different interface. Then just do a command line like "ifconfig" and figure out the name of your interfaces. Then go into your software and tell it to only use that interface. Again, your software might not have that feature, but maybe it does.
